questions.answer: Case 1: $3x+1=x-5\Rightarrow2x=-6\Rightarrow x=-3$. Case 2: $3x+1=-(x-5)\Rightarrow4x=4\Rightarrow x=1$. Both check: solutions $x=-3$ or $x=1$.
$|x-4|=7$, so $x-4=7\Rightarrow x=11$, or $x-4=-7\Rightarrow x=-3$. Solutions: $x=11$ or $x=-3$.

questions.q: Use the remainder theorem to find the remainder when $f(x)=x^3+2x^2-5x+1$ is divided by $(x-2)$.

parts: Use the factor theorem to show that $(x+3)$ is a factor of $f(x)$.

questions.q: Divide $x^3-2x^2-5x+6$ by $(x-3)$ using polynomial long division. State the quotient and remainder.

questions.answer: $\log_2\left[(x+1)(x-1)\right]=3\Rightarrow x^2-1=8\Rightarrow x^2=9\Rightarrow x=\pm3$. Since $x>1$ is required for $\log_2(x-1)$ to be defined, reject $x=-3$. Solution: $x=3$.
$\log_5(x^2)=\log_5 16\Rightarrow x^2=16\Rightarrow x=\pm4$. Since $x>0$ is required, reject $x=-4$. Solution: $x=4$.

questions.q: Solve $2^x=15$ for $x$, giving your answer to three decimal places.

questions.answer: $x^2-4x+3=-x+3\Rightarrow x^2-3x=0\Rightarrow x(x-3)=0\Rightarrow x=0$ or $x=3$. Solutions: $(0,3)$ and $(3,0)$.

Multiply through by $(x-2)(x+2)$: $x(x+2)+2(x-2)=8\Rightarrow x^2+4x-4=8\Rightarrow x^2+4x-12=0\Rightarrow(x+6)(x-2)=0\Rightarrow x=-6$ or $x=2$. Since $x=2$ makes the denominator zero, it is extraneous. Solution: $x=-6$.

sections.heading: Systems of inequalities and linear programming

questions.q: A feasible region is bounded by the constraints $x\geq0$, $y\geq0$, $x+y\leq6$, and $2x+y\leq10$. Find the vertices of the feasible region.
questions.answer: Intersecting boundary lines pairwise (and checking each candidate point satisfies every constraint) gives vertices $(0,0)$, $(5,0)$, $(4,2)$, and $(0,6)$.

questions.q: Using the feasible region from the previous question, find the maximum value of $P=3x+2y$ over the region, and state where it occurs.
questions.answer: Evaluating $P$ at each vertex: $(0,0)\to0$; $(5,0)\to15$; $(4,2)\to16$; $(0,6)\to12$. The maximum is $P=16$, occurring at $(4,2)$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: production planning at a furniture workshop

questions.q: This question has three parts. A furniture workshop makes tables and chairs. Each table requires 4 hours of carpentry and 2 hours of finishing; each chair requires 1 hour of carpentry and 1 hour of finishing. Each week the shop has at most 32 hours of carpentry time and 20 hours of finishing time available. Each table earns a profit of 70 dollars and each chair earns a profit of 30 dollars. Let $x$ be the number of tables and $y$ the number of chairs produced in a week. (a) Write the system of inequalities describing the constraints (including $x\geq0$ and $y\geq0$). (b) Find the vertices of the feasible region. (c) Determine the number of tables and chairs that maximizes the weekly profit $P=70x+30y$, and find the maximum profit.
questions.answer: (a) The constraints are $x\geq0$, $y\geq0$, $4x+y\leq32$ (carpentry), and $2x+y\leq20$ (finishing). (b) The boundary lines meet the axes and each other at $(0,0)$, $(8,0)$, $(6,8)$, and $(0,20)$ — these are the vertices of the feasible region. (c) Evaluating $P=70x+30y$: $(0,0)\to0$; $(8,0)\to560$; $(6,8)\to660$; $(0,20)\to600$. The maximum profit is $660$ dollars, achieved by producing $6$ tables and $8$ chairs per week.
